cashTip: Cards work almost everywhere; carry a little cash for beach bars and markets.
name: Ibiza
tagline: Famous clubs, quiet coves and a walled old town
summary: Ibiza is two islands in one: the world's most famous club scene and a gentle Mediterranean island of pine-backed coves, whitewashed villages and sunset bars. Its walled old town, Dalt Vila, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
seasonNote: Clubs open from late May to early October. July and August are hot, crowded and expensive; June and September are the sweet spot.
arrival: Ibiza Airport is 15 minutes from Ibiza Town. Ferries run from Barcelona, Valencia, Dénia and Palma.
gettingAround: Buses link the main towns and beaches; rent a car or scooter to reach the quieter coves.
foodTip: Bullit de peix fish stew, arroz a banda and flaó cheesecake.
buyTip: Hippy-market crafts at Las Dalias and Es Canar, and Ibiza salt.
baseArea: Ibiza Town or Santa Eulària for calm; San Antonio for party

connections.note: Many daily flights; overnight ferries too.

items.name: Dalt Vila
items.summary: Renaissance walls wrapping a hilltop old town with a cathedral and sea views.
flow: Enter by Portal de ses Taules.

items.name: Cala Comte sunset
items.summary: Turquoise shallows and rocky islets facing the island's best sunset.
items.tip: Bring a towel and stay for sunset.

items.name: Es Vedrà viewpoint
items.summary: A towering limestone islet wrapped in myth, seen from the cliffs at Torre des Savinar.
items.expect: A short hike from the car park.
flow: Watch the sun drop behind Es Vedrà.

items.name: Ses Salines
items.summary: Salt flats, flamingos and a long sandy beach in a protected park.
items.expect: Beach clubs at one end; wild dunes at the other.
items.tip: Walk to Es Cavallet for calmer sand.

items.name: Superclubs
items.summary: World-famous clubs like Ushuaïa, Hï and Pacha with top DJs.
flow: Move on to Hï or Pacha.

items.name: Las Dalias hippy market
items.summary: Ibiza's hippy heritage: crafts, clothes and music, plus a night market in summer.
items.expect: Saturdays all year; night market on summer evenings.

items.name: Inland villages
items.summary: Whitewashed churches and village squares among almond and olive groves.
items.expect: Slow pace; cafés on the square.

items.name: Formentera day trip
items.summary: A 30-minute ferry to Caribbean-clear water at Ses Illetes.
items.expect: Ferries from Ibiza Town; rent a bike or scooter there.
items.tip: Go early to beat the crowds.

items.name: Bullit de peix
items.summary: Fish stewed with potatoes, then rice cooked in the broth.
items.tip: Try it at a cove restaurant like Es Boldado.

items.name: Flaó
items.summary: A mint-scented cheesecake made with sheep's and goat's cheese.

items.name: Beach chiringuitos
items.summary: Grilled fish and sangria with your feet in the sand.

cashTip: Cards work almost everywhere; carry a little cash for beach bars and markets.
name: Tenerife
tagline: Spain's highest peak above year-round sunshine
summary: Tenerife is the largest Canary Island, with spring weather all year. Ride the cable car up Mount Teide, Spain's highest peak, walk volcanic moonscapes, see whales offshore and explore colonial La Laguna.
seasonNote: Warm all year. Winter is high season for northern Europeans; Carnival in February is one of the world's biggest.
arrival: Tenerife South Airport serves the resorts; Tenerife North is near La Laguna. Flights from across Europe.
gettingAround: Good TITSA buses; rent a car to reach Teide and the northwest.
foodTip: Papas arrugadas with mojo sauce, grilled cheese and fresh fish in guachinches.
buyTip: Canarian wine, mojo sauces and aloe vera products.
baseArea: Puerto de la Cruz or Costa Adeje

items.name: Teide National Park
items.summary: Spain's highest peak, 3,715 m, rising from a vast volcanic crater.
items.expect: Cable car to near the top; summit permit needed for the last stretch.
items.tip: Book the cable car and permit online.

items.name: Teide stargazing
items.summary: Some of Europe's clearest skies, with guided telescope tours.

items.name: Masca village and gorge
items.summary: A tiny village clinging to a ravine in the Teno mountains.
items.expect: The gorge hike needs booking; the road is twisty.

items.name: Los Gigantes cliffs
items.summary: Sheer 600 m cliffs best seen from a boat.
items.expect: Boat trips include dolphin and whale watching.
items.tip: Pick a small boat with a swim stop.

items.name: San Cristóbal de La Laguna
items.summary: A UNESCO colonial town whose grid inspired cities across Latin America.
items.tip: Visit the cathedral and Plaza del Adelantado.

items.name: Anaga Rural Park
items.summary: Ancient laurel forest, misty ridges and black-sand beaches.
items.expect: Cool and damp in the forest.
items.tip: Walk the Sendero de los Sentidos.

items.name: Loro Parque
items.summary: A big zoo with parrots, penguins and orcas.

items.name: Papas arrugadas con mojo
items.summary: Salt-crusted wrinkled potatoes with red and green mojo sauces.

items.name: Guachinches
items.summary: Family-run wine-farm eateries serving home cooking with their own wine.
items.tip: Look for hand-written signs in the north.

items.name: Fresh fish in harbours
items.summary: Grilled vieja and cherne in harbour restaurants at Los Abrigos.

cashTip: Cards work almost everywhere; small cash helps at markets and bakeries.
name: Marseille
tagline: France's oldest city, gritty and sunny on the sea
summary: Marseille is France's oldest city and its great Mediterranean port: noisy, multicultural and full of light. Climb to Notre-Dame de la Garde, wander the Panier quarter, eat bouillabaisse at the Old Port and hike to white limestone calanques.
seasonNote: Summer is hot; calanques may close in high fire risk. The mistral wind can blow cold in winter and spring.
arrival: Trains from Paris take about 3 hours 20; Marseille Provence Airport has shuttle buses to Saint-Charles station.
gettingAround: Metro, trams and buses; boats to the Frioul islands and calanques.
foodTip: Bouillabaisse, panisse chickpea fries and navette biscuits.
buyTip: Savon de Marseille soap and santons figurines.

items.name: Notre-Dame de la Garde
items.summary: A golden-Virgin basilica above the city with sweeping views.
items.expect: Bus 60 or a steep walk up.
items.tip: Go late afternoon for the light.

items.name: Vieux-Port
items.summary: The old harbour with fish sellers, cafés and the mirrored Ombrière canopy.

items.name: Le Panier
items.summary: Marseille's oldest quarter of steep lanes, street art and the Vieille Charité.

items.name: MuCEM and Fort Saint-Jean
items.wiki: Museum of European and Mediterranean Civilisations
items.summary: A lace-concrete museum linked by footbridge to a medieval fort.
items.expect: The fort and rooftop are free.

items.name: Calanques National Park
items.summary: White limestone cliffs and turquoise inlets like Sugiton and En-Vau.
items.expect: Hike or take a boat; some close on high fire-risk days.
items.why: Wild coast right by the city.

items.name: Château d'If
items.summary: An island fortress-prison made famous by The Count of Monte Cristo.

items.name: Cassis day trip
items.summary: A pretty fishing port with boat tours of the calanques and white wine.
items.tip: Take a calanques boat from the port.

items.name: Bouillabaisse
items.summary: The famous fish stew: broth with rouille-topped croutons, then the fish.
items.expect: Real versions cost €60+; beware cheap ones.
items.tip: Book at a restaurant signing the Bouillabaisse charter.

items.name: Panisse
items.summary: Crisp fried chickpea fingers, a street snack by the sea.

items.name: Noailles market
items.summary: A North African-style market of spices, flatbreads and stalls.

cashTip: Cards work almost everywhere; carry a few euros for fries stands and markets.
name: Bruges
tagline: A fairy-tale medieval town of canals
summary: Bruges is one of Europe's best-preserved medieval towns: cobbled lanes, gabled houses, quiet canals and a towering belfry. It's a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the home of Flemish Primitive painting, lace, chocolate and beer.
seasonNote: Day-trippers crowd the centre from late morning; stay overnight for quiet evenings. Christmas markets in December.
arrival: Trains from Brussels take about 1 hour, and from Ghent 25 minutes.
gettingAround: Walk or cycle; canal boats run from several jetties.
foodTip: Mussels and fries, Flemish stew and waffles.

items.name: Markt and Belfry
items.summary: The main square with a 13th-century belfry; climb 366 steps for the view.

items.name: Canal boat tour
items.summary: Half-hour boat rides under bridges past gabled houses.

items.name: Burg and Basilica of the Holy Blood
items.summary: A square of grand civic buildings and a chapel holding a relic of Christ's blood.

items.name: Groeninge Museum
items.summary: Flemish Primitives including Van Eyck's Madonna with Canon van der Paele.

items.name: Church of Our Lady
items.summary: Home to Michelangelo's Madonna and Child.
items.expect: Small fee for the museum part.

items.name: Beguinage and Minnewater
items.summary: A quiet white-walled courtyard and the 'Lake of Love'.

items.name: Windmills on the ramparts
items.summary: Working windmills along the green city walls.

items.name: Mussels and fries
items.summary: Steaming pots of mussels with fries and mayonnaise.

items.name: Chocolatiers
items.summary: Pralines from small makers along the lanes.

items.name: Beer cafés
items.summary: Brewery tours and bars with hundreds of Belgian beers.
items.tip: Try Brugse Zot at De Halve Maan.

cashTip: Cards are widely accepted; buses take cards or the Tallinja card, and small kiosks like cash.
name: Valletta · Malta
tagline: A golden fortress capital in the heart of the Mediterranean
summary: Valletta, Malta's tiny honey-stone capital, was built by the Knights of St John and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. From here explore the Grand Harbour, Caravaggio, prehistoric temples older than the pyramids, and the blue waters of Gozo and Comino.
seasonNote: Hot summers; spring and autumn are ideal. Village festas fill summer weekends.
arrival: Malta International Airport is 20 minutes away by bus or taxi. Ferries from Sicily.
gettingAround: Walk Valletta; buses cover the island; ferries to the Three Cities, Sliema and Gozo.
foodTip: Pastizzi, rabbit stew and ftira sandwiches.
buyTip: Maltese lace, filigree silver and Mdina glass.

connections.note: Or a ferry to Pozzallo then a drive.

items.name: St John's Co-Cathedral
items.summary: A plain facade hiding a dazzling gilded interior and Caravaggio's Beheading of St John.

items.name: Upper Barrakka Gardens
items.summary: Arcaded gardens with the best view of the Grand Harbour; a cannon fires at noon.
items.tip: Be there at 12:00 for the gun salute.

items.name: Three Cities
items.summary: Older fortified towns across the harbour, reached by a traditional dgħajsa boat.

items.name: Mdina
items.summary: A silent walled hilltop city, Malta's old capital.
items.tip: Visit at dusk when it's quiet.

items.name: Ħal Saflieni Hypogeum
items.summary: A 5,000-year-old underground temple and burial site.
items.expect: Only 80 visitors a day; book weeks ahead.
items.tip: Book as soon as you have dates.

items.name: Comino Blue Lagoon
items.summary: Startlingly clear turquoise water between two islands.

items.name: Gozo day trip
items.summary: Malta's greener sister island with the Citadel of Victoria and Ġgantija temples.
items.tip: Rent a car or hop-on bus.

items.name: Pastizzi
items.summary: Flaky pastries filled with ricotta or peas, about 50 cents each.

items.name: Stuffat tal-fenek
items.summary: Rabbit stewed in wine and garlic, the national dish.
items.tip: Try it in a village restaurant.

items.name: Ftira
items.summary: Ring-shaped Maltese bread stuffed with tuna, tomato and capers.

cashTip: Montenegro uses the euro. Cards work in hotels and bigger restaurants; carry cash for boats, taxis and small cafés.
name: Kotor
tagline: A walled town at the end of a fjord-like bay
summary: Kotor is a medieval walled town tucked at the end of the Bay of Kotor, below steep mountains. Climb the fortress walls for a famous view, wander marble lanes full of cats and churches, and boat to island churches and baroque Perast.
seasonNote: Cruise ships crowd the old town in summer; check cruise days. Spring and autumn are calmer.
arrival: Tivat Airport is 20 minutes away; Dubrovnik Airport about 1.5 hours with a border crossing.
gettingAround: Walk the old town; buses and boats around the bay; rent a car for the mountains.
foodTip: Black risotto, mussels from the bay and Njeguši ham and cheese.
buyTip: Local olive oil, Vranac wine and Njeguši prosciutto.

connections.note: Border crossing; can be slow in summer.

items.name: Fortress of San Giovanni
items.summary: Some 1,350 steps up the town walls to a fortress high above the bay.
items.expect: Hot and steep; go early or late.
items.tip: Start at dawn for cool air and light.
flow: Church of Our Lady of Remedy.

items.name: Old town
items.summary: A maze of squares, palaces and Romanesque churches inside the walls.
items.tip: Explore early or after ships leave.

items.name: St Tryphon's Cathedral
items.summary: A 12th-century Romanesque cathedral with frescoes and a treasury.

items.name: Perast and Our Lady of the Rocks
items.summary: A baroque village and an artificial island church reached by boat.

items.name: Ladder of Kotor and Lovćen
items.summary: Hairpin road up to Lovćen and the Njegoš mausoleum high above the bay.

items.name: Blue Cave boat trip
items.summary: A sea cave glowing blue on sunny days, with swims at bay beaches.

items.name: Budva old town
items.summary: A walled seaside town and beaches on the open coast.

items.name: Bay seafood
items.summary: Black risotto with cuttlefish ink and mussels from bay farms.

items.name: Njeguški pršut
items.summary: Smoked mountain ham and cheese from Njeguši village.

items.name: Burek
items.summary: Flaky pastry filled with cheese or meat, with yogurt.

cashTip: Cards work almost everywhere; keep coins for church lights and espresso bars.
name: Pisa
tagline: The Leaning Tower and a lively university town
summary: Pisa is famous for its Leaning Tower, part of the white-marble Piazza dei Miracoli. Beyond the tower, it's a lively university town on the Arno with Renaissance squares and an easy base for Lucca and the Tuscan coast.
seasonNote: Busy with day-trippers in summer; book tower slots ahead.
arrival: Pisa Airport is 5 minutes from the centre; trains from Florence take about an hour.
foodTip: Cecina chickpea flatbread and Tuscan soups.
buyTip: Leather from Florence-style shops and Tuscan wine.

items.name: Leaning Tower
items.summary: Climb 251 steps up the famous tilted bell tower.
items.tip: Book online a few days ahead.

items.name: Cathedral and Baptistery
items.summary: Romanesque cathedral and the largest baptistery in Italy, with a singing echo.
items.tip: Wait for the baptistery echo demonstration.

items.name: Camposanto
items.summary: A marble cloister cemetery with restored medieval frescoes.
items.tip: See the Triumph of Death fresco.

items.name: Piazza dei Cavalieri
items.summary: A Renaissance square with the sgraffito palace of the Scuola Normale.

items.name: Lungarno and Santa Maria della Spina
items.summary: A tiny Gothic church on the river and pastel palazzi along the Arno.

items.name: Lucca day trip
items.summary: A walled town where you can cycle the tree-lined ramparts.
items.tip: Rent a bike for the walls.

items.name: Cecina
items.summary: Thin chickpea-flour flatbread, eaten hot in a focaccia.
items.expect: Pizzerias sell it by the slice.

items.name: Tuscan trattorie
items.summary: Ribollita, pici pasta and wild boar ragù.

items.name: Gelato
items.summary: Artisan gelato along the arcaded Borgo Stretto.
